claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.

In AWS CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a newer execution can overtake an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping the waiting execution before it ever starts (the lock only protects an execution once it is actually running).

If a CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` is busy and enough commits land, a queued CodePipeline execution waiting behind it can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment rather than colliding with one already in progress.
Setting an AWS CodePipeline pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue so each one runs in turn rather than being superseded by a later execution.
AWS CodePipeline's `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (`pipelineType` V2).
When defining a CodePipeline pipeline that uses `QUEUED` execution mode, both `executionMode` and `pipelineType` must be set, via the AWS CLI's `create-pipeline`/`update-pipeline` commands.
The Pulumi `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.

The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource is described further below in the same page, in the 'Manage the pipeline with Pulumi' section, and its API docs exist at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/codepipeline/pipeline/.
The AWS CodePipeline user guide page 'concepts-how-it-works' documents pipeline execution modes including `SUPERSEDED`.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other run's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that can prevent concurrent deployment runs targeting that environment.
The Azure Pipelines exclusive lock check is documented at the Microsoft Learn 'approvals' page (https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/devops/pipelines/process/approvals?view=azure-devops).
The link target /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists and describes Pulumi update conflicts.
In Azure DevOps, an exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` is set at the stage level to control how the exclusive lock check on a referenced environment treats queued runs.
The Azure Pipelines `lockBehavior` stage property accepts the values `sequential` and `runLatest`.
The Azure Pipelines `Pulumi@1` task accepts inputs `command: up`, `stack`, and `args` (e.g. `args: --yes`), with stack given in the form `org/project/stack`.
`runLatest` is the default value of `lockBehavior` in Azure Pipelines.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and an older run waiting behind it is passed over (cancelled/skipped) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage run acquires the exclusive lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud itself serializes updates to a stack, running them one at a time in order.

`runLatest` is acceptable for a preview environment where only the newest state matters, but not for a stack where every update needs to land; `sequential` is recommended instead for deployment stacks.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a resource `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` that manages the exclusive lock check as code.
The link target /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/ exists in the Pulumi Registry.
When two runs of the same build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them.
When two concurrent runs target the same Pulumi stack, the run that does not get the lease has its `pulumi up` fail with an update conflict error.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available (no concurrency limit by default).
The link target /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ (Pulumi update conflicts troubleshooting page) exists.
TeamCity build configurations have an advanced option named "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" located under the configuration's General Settings.
The default value of TeamCity's "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" option is 0, which means unlimited.

Setting TeamCity's "Limit the number of simultaneously running builds" to 1 causes a second build that would otherwise start immediately to be queued behind the first and to run only once the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud has a per-stack lease that gives one-at-a-time update behavior for a stack.
Limiting TeamCity concurrent builds to 1 prevents the build from reaching the point of hitting a Pulumi update conflict, because it queues builds earlier than Pulumi Cloud's per-stack lease.

In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment that the deployment job targets, together with `lockBehavior: sequential` on the stage, serializes Pulumi deployments so they do not run concurrently.
Azure Pipelines supports an 'exclusive lock' check that can be added to an environment.
Azure Pipelines YAML stages accept a `lockBehavior` property with a `sequential` value.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section anchored at '#serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
In AWS CodePipeline, setting the pipeline's execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions run in turn.
AWS CodePipeline supports a pipeline execution mode setting with a `QUEUED` value.
The default AWS CodePipeline execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section anchored at '#serialize-pipeline-executions'.
In TeamCity, setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' to 1 on the build configuration serializes Pulumi deployment builds.
TeamCity build configurations have a setting named 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds'.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section anchored at '#limit-concurrent-builds' that describes this setting.
